title: How do Spring, JPA, and JUnit use annotations at runtime?
shortTitle: How do Spring, JPA, and JUnit use annotations at runtime?
keyPoints: Spring: @Component, @Autowired, @Transactional – discovered via classpath scanning, processed via reflection/CGLIB proxies
JPA: @Entity, @Table, @Column, @Id – Hibernate reads annotations to map classes to database tables
JUnit: @Test, @BeforeEach, @ParameterizedTest – test runner discovers methods via reflection
All require @Retention(RUNTIME) – annotations must survive into the running JVM
Spring AOP creates proxies around @Transactional methods to manage transaction begin/commit/rollback

s1_definition.oneliner: Spring uses reflection to discover @Component beans and create proxies for @Transactional. JPA reads @Entity/@Column to map objects to database tables. JUnit discovers @Test methods via reflection.
s1_definition.profdef:
Framework annotation processing:

- **Spring:** Scans classpath for @Component/@Service/@Repository. Uses reflection to read @Autowired for dependency injection. Creates CGLIB proxies for @Transactional.
- **JPA:** Hibernate reads @Entity, @Table, @Column, @Id at startup to build the mapping between Java objects and database tables.
- **JUnit:** The test runner scans for methods annotated with @Test, @BeforeEach, @AfterEach and invokes them via reflection.
s1_definition.analogy: Annotations are labels on boxes in a warehouse. Spring's scanner walks through the warehouse reading labels to decide how to wire things together. JPA's mapper reads labels to know which box goes on which shelf (table). JUnit's runner reads "test" labels to know which boxes to open and verify.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Spring, JPA, and JUnit all use annotations with RUNTIME retention, processed via reflection. Spring scans for @Component to create beans, reads @Autowired for injection, and wraps @Transactional methods in proxy-managed transactions. JPA reads @Entity and @Column to map objects to database tables. JUnit discovers @Test methods to build the test suite.

One sentence to remember: framework annotations need RUNTIME retention so reflection can discover and process them – Spring for DI/AOP, JPA for ORM, JUnit for test discovery.
